method: Every field was taken from a source fetched on 2026-09-12. Nothing was inferred from "countries like this usually ...". Norway is the deliberate canary: euMember is false (EEA/EFTA, not the EU), natoMember is true (founding member, 1949) and recognisesKosovo is true (28 March 2008). recognisesKosovo / recognitionDate / diplomaticRelationsKosovo come from the maintained per-state recognition table at en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_recognition_of_Kosovo, whose rows are individually cited to national foreign ministries. The Republic of Kosovo MFA page was fetched as well, but it publishes only a headline count and no machine-readable per-state list, so it is cited for the official count and Kosovo position rather than for per-country dates. The four 2025 recognitions (Kenya, Sudan, Syria, the Bahamas) were each re-checked against independent news reporting. euMember / euAccessionYear come from the European Union country profiles on europa.eu (27 member states). natoMember / natoAccessionYear come from NATO’s own "Member countries" page (32 member states with accession dates). bombedBelgrade1999 is NOT derived from NATO membership. NATO’s own Kosovo Air Campaign page gives the operation and its dates but names no participants, so the participant list comes from Air & Space Forces Magazine ("Thirteen of NATO’s 19 nations sent aircraft to take part ... NATO’s three newest members - Poland, Hungary, and the Czech Republic - did not join in. Greece, Iceland, and Luxembourg also abstained."), cross-checked against the per-nation aircraft breakdown in the Wikipedia "NATO forces" section. The thirteen: Belgium, Canada, Denmark, France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Norway, Portugal, Spain, Turkiye, the United Kingdom and the United States. sanctionedSerbia1990s rests on UNSCR 757 (30 May 1992), which decided that ALL States shall apply the embargo on the FRY, and UNSCR 820 (17 April 1993), which strengthened it. For a UN member the honest reading is "implemented a binding UN obligation", not "chose to punish Serbia", so the basis is recorded per country in sanctionedSerbia1990sBasis: "un" = UN member bound from 30 May 1992; "un-late" = admitted to the UN part-way through the embargo; "autonomous" = not a UN member but implemented it anyway (Switzerland); "target" = was inside the FRY.

caveats.recognitionCountIsContested: There is no single agreed number. The Republic of Kosovo counts about 121 recognitions (Syria was announced as the 120th in October 2025 and the Bahamas as the 121st in December 2025); independent monitors count 110 UN member states plus Taiwan, the Cook Islands and Niue; Serbia claims the real figure is in the mid-80s because of withdrawn recognitions. This dataset uses the per-state list behind the 110 figure and records the disagreement here rather than silently picking a side.
caveats.withdrawnRecognitions: Eight states are documented as having withdrawn recognition (Burundi, Papua New Guinea, Dominica, the Solomon Islands, Madagascar, Togo, the Central African Republic and Nauru), and Serbia claims six more (Grenada, Guinea-Bissau, Liberia, Palau, Sao Tome and Principe, Suriname) which Kosovo’s foreign ministry calls propaganda. None of those states issue a GS1 barcode prefix in data/gs1-prefixes.json, so none of them appear in this table and the dispute changes no value here.
caveats.sanctionsAreNotAVerdict: sanctionedSerbia1990s being true for almost every country is NOT evidence that almost every country singled Serbia out. It reflects a binding Chapter VII obligation on every UN member under UNSCR 757/820. Read sanctionedSerbia1990sBasis before drawing any conclusion. The embargo was suspended by UNSCR 1022 (22 November 1995) and terminated by UNSCR 1074 (1 October 1996).
caveats.membershipIsNotParticipation: bombedBelgrade1999 is about Operation Allied Force specifically. Six of the nineteen NATO members of 1999 took no part in it. Hungary is the sharpest case: it contributed no aircraft, yet NATO launched strikes from Hungarian airfields. Albania and North Macedonia were not NATO members and flew nothing, but NATO forces operated from their territory.
caveats.notSovereignStates: Hong Kong and Macau issue their own GS1 prefixes but are not sovereign states, and Kosovo (XK) is the subject of the checklist rather than an assessor of it. These three carry nulls and verified:false.
caveats.euNonRecognisers: Five EU member states do not recognise Kosovo: Spain, Greece, Cyprus, Romania and Slovakia. All five are in this table with recognisesKosovo:false.
caveats.freshness: Recognition is a moving target: four states recognised Kosovo during 2025 after a five-year gap. Re-check this file against its sources before relying on it.
